main_body: Half-timbered house: a large hip/gable tile roof over plaster-and-timber front walls, with a front gable wing and a door in the lower wing.
top_band: Terracotta tile roof slope, light-to-dark orange/red with a highlighted ridge, rows ~1-26 on the main body (the front gable extends to ~row 45). It is clearly a sloped surface seen from above.
evidence: Reading a column through the main body: tile roof slope (rows ~1-26), then a dark eave line at rows ~26-27 that shades the wall. Below it is the plaster and timber front face (rows ~27-44), with timber frames, a window with a sill, and a door set into the timber frame. The gable wing has its own roof slope above a triangular wall. The roof is a large visible top surface and the walls are a distinct south face, as in the Beodeul house references.

style.evidence: The roof tiles have per-tile highlights across about five tone steps, from a pale yellow ridge to deep brown-red. Outlines are dark brown or red-brown beside wood and tiles, not neutral black. The plaster has speckle dots and the timber has grain. The chimney is shaded brick. Tile density matches the Beodeul house references, so it would sit beside them without looking thinner.
